decry|descry.distinction: To decry is to denounce something publicly, while to descry is to catch sight of something at a distance.

defer|deter.distinction: To defer is to postpone, or to yield to another's judgement, while to deter is to discourage someone from acting at all.

deflect|reflect.distinction: To deflect is to turn something aside, including a question, while to reflect is to think deeply or to show something back.

deign|feign.distinction: To deign is to condescend to do something beneath you, while to feign is to pretend to a feeling or condition you do not have.

delegate|relegate.distinction: To delegate is to entrust a task to someone else, while to relegate is to push a person or thing down to a lower position.

demur|demure.distinction: To demur is to object or hesitate politely, while demure is an adjective for a modest and reserved manner.

denounce|renounce.distinction: To denounce is to condemn something publicly, while to renounce is to give up a claim or belief of your own.

depose|repose.distinction: To depose is to remove a ruler from office or to testify on oath, while repose is a noun meaning restful calm.

deride|derive.distinction: To deride is to mock someone scornfully, while to derive is to obtain or trace something from its source.

despite|respite.distinction: Despite usually means in spite of, and as a noun means contempt, while a respite is a short break from something hard.

disparage|disparate.distinction: To disparage is to belittle something, while disparate is an adjective meaning fundamentally different in kind.

dispense|disperse.distinction: To dispense is to hand something out, while to disperse is for a crowd or a mist to scatter and go in all directions.

disport|distort.distinction: To disport is to amuse oneself and frolic, while to distort is to twist a shape or a meaning away from the truth.

dissemble|dissembler.distinction: To dissemble is to conceal your real motives, while a dissembler is the person who habitually does it.

divert|divest.distinction: To divert is to redirect something or to entertain, while to divest is to rid yourself of a holding by selling or shedding it.

egress|regress.distinction: Egress is the way out or the act of leaving, while to regress is to slip back into an earlier and worse condition.

enchant|penchant.distinction: To enchant is to delight someone as if by a spell, while a penchant is a settled liking or tendency someone has.

endue|ensue.distinction: To endue is to invest someone with a quality, while to ensue is for something to follow as a consequence.

euphoria|euphoric.distinction: Euphoria is the state of intense elation, while euphoric is the adjective describing a person or mood in that state.

exhort|extort.distinction: To exhort is to urge someone strongly to act, while to extort is to take money or a concession by threat.

expatiate|expatriate.distinction: To expatiate is to speak or write at great length, while an expatriate is a person living outside their own country.

extant|sextant.distinction: Extant means still surviving in existence, while a sextant is the navigational instrument for measuring angles at sea.

facetious|factious.distinction: Facetious means joking when the moment calls for seriousness, while factious means given to splitting a group into quarrelling parties.

factious|fractious.distinction: Factious describes a group that splits into rival camps, while fractious describes a person or body that is irritable and hard to manage.

fester|foster.distinction: To fester is for a wound or a grievance to worsen while ignored, while to foster is to nurture something so it grows.

flail|flair.distinction: To flail is to wave about wildly and achieve nothing, while a flair is a natural talent that makes the doing look easy.

flounder|founder.distinction: To flounder is to struggle clumsily while still afloat, while to founder is to go down altogether; talks flounder before they founder.

foment|moment.distinction: To foment is to stir up trouble deliberately, while a moment is an instant of time, or in formal use the importance of a matter.

fortify|mortify.distinction: To fortify is to strengthen something against attack, while to mortify is to humiliate someone deeply.

garble|warble.distinction: To garble is to distort a message so the sense is lost, while to warble is to sing with trilling changes of pitch.

generate|venerate.distinction: To generate is to bring something into existence, while to venerate is to regard a person or thing with deep respect.

genial|venial.distinction: Genial describes a warm and friendly manner, while venial describes a fault small enough to be forgiven.

graft|grant.distinction: Graft is corruption by someone in office, while to grant is to bestow something or to concede a point in argument.

gratify|ratify.distinction: To gratify is to please someone or satisfy a desire, while to ratify is to give a treaty or agreement formal approval.

grove|grovel.distinction: A grove is a small stand of trees, while to grovel is to abase yourself before someone in the hope of favour.

gusto|gusty.distinction: Gusto is hearty enjoyment in doing something, while gusty describes wind arriving in sudden blasts.

hardy|harry.distinction: Hardy describes something tough enough to endure hard conditions, while to harry is to harass someone persistently.

harry|parry.distinction: To harry is to keep attacking or pestering, while to parry is to turn a single blow or question aside.

harry|tarry.distinction: To harry is to harass someone without letting up, while to tarry is simply to linger and delay.

hedonism|hedonist.distinction: Hedonism is the doctrine that pleasure is the highest good, while a hedonist is the person who lives by it.

heretic|hermetic.distinction: A heretic holds a doctrine the orthodox reject, while hermetic means sealed against anything getting in or out.

hound|sound.distinction: To hound someone is to pursue them relentlessly, while sound as an adjective means solid, reliable and free of defect.

imperious|impervious.distinction: Imperious describes an arrogant commanding manner, while impervious means nothing gets through, whether water or criticism.

imprudent|impudent.distinction: Imprudent is a failure of judgement, while impudent is a failure of manners; an imprudent loan, an impudent reply.

indolent|insolent.distinction: Indolent means habitually lazy, while insolent means openly disrespectful; one will not work, the other will not defer.

inept|inert.distinction: Inept means clumsy and incompetent at doing something, while inert means not acting or reacting at all.

infer|inter.distinction: To infer is to draw a conclusion from evidence, while to inter is to bury a body in the ground.

ingenious|ingenuous.distinction: Ingenious means cleverly inventive, while ingenuous means innocent and unsuspecting; the two are almost opposite in what they say about a person.

insidious|invidious.distinction: Insidious harm works unnoticed until it is advanced, while an invidious choice is one that will cause resentment whichever way it goes.

insolent|insolvent.distinction: Insolent means rudely disrespectful, while insolvent means unable to pay what is owed.

jingoism|jingoist.distinction: Jingoism is aggressive boastful patriotism as a doctrine, while a jingoist is the person who preaches it.

knell|knoll.distinction: A knell is the slow bell that marks an ending, while a knoll is a small rounded hill.

lament|latent.distinction: To lament is to mourn something aloud, while latent describes a quality present but not yet showing itself.

latent|patent.distinction: Latent means present but not yet visible, while patent means so obvious that nobody needs it pointed out.

latitude|platitude.distinction: Latitude is freedom to act as you judge best, while a platitude is a stale remark offered as though it were wisdom.

levee|level.distinction: A levee is the bank that holds a river back, while to level is to aim an accusation at someone or to flatten something.

loath|loathe.distinction: Loath is an adjective meaning reluctant, while to loathe is a verb meaning to hate intensely; the final e marks the verb.

lucid|lurid.distinction: Lucid means clear and easy to follow, while lurid means shockingly vivid and sensational.

luminous|numinous.distinction: Luminous means giving off light, while numinous means suggesting the presence of something divine.

martial|partial.distinction: Martial means relating to war and the military, while partial means biased toward one side, or covering only part of something.

matriarch|patriarch.distinction: A matriarch is the woman who heads a family or group, while a patriarch is the man who does; the roles differ only in sex.

mettlesome|nettlesome.distinction: Mettlesome means spirited and brave, while nettlesome means irritating and troublesome to deal with.

mettle|nettle.distinction: Mettle is the courage a person proves under test, while to nettle is to irritate someone into a reaction.

naive|waive.distinction: Naive means lacking experience and too ready to trust, while to waive is to give up a right you could have enforced.

nihilism|nihilist.distinction: Nihilism is the doctrine that nothing has meaning, while a nihilist is the person who holds it.

odium|podium.distinction: Odium is the widespread hatred directed at someone, while a podium is the raised platform a speaker stands on.

parry|tarry.distinction: To parry is to deflect a blow or a question, while to tarry is to linger and put off leaving.

perpetrate|perpetuate.distinction: To perpetrate is to commit a wrong, while to perpetuate is to keep something going; a myth is perpetuated, a fraud is perpetrated.

policy|polity.distinction: A policy is the course of action an organisation adopts, while a polity is an organised political community considered as a whole.

prone|prune.distinction: Prone means liable to something or lying face down, while to prune is to cut something back so what remains does better.

prude|prune.distinction: A prude is easily shocked by anything improper, while to prune is to trim something back.

pugilism|pugilist.distinction: Pugilism is the sport of boxing, while a pugilist is the fighter who practises it.

ramify|ratify.distinction: To ramify is to branch out into further complications, while to ratify is to approve something formally so it takes effect.

rampant|rampart.distinction: Rampant describes something spreading with nothing to check it, while a rampart is the defensive wall built to check an attack.

rebus|rebut.distinction: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures stand for words, while to rebut is to answer an argument with counter-evidence.

redress|regress.distinction: Redress is the remedy given for a wrong, while to regress is to slip back to an earlier and worse state.

refine|repine.distinction: To refine is to improve something by small careful changes, while to repine is to fret and complain about your lot.

render|tender.distinction: To render is to cause something to become so, or to provide it, while to tender is to offer something formally, such as a resignation.

revere|reverie.distinction: To revere is to hold someone in deep respect, while a reverie is a daydream you drift into.

rigor|vigor.distinction: Rigor is strict thoroughness or harshness in method, while vigor is energy and strength in carrying something out.

slake|stake.distinction: To slake is to satisfy a thirst or a desire, while a stake is something risked, or an interest held in an outcome.

sleight|slight.distinction: Sleight is skilled trickery of the hands, as in sleight of hand, while to slight someone is to snub them.

stark|start.distinction: Stark means bare and severe, while to start in this sense is to jump in surprise at something sudden.

sully|surly.distinction: To sully is to stain a reputation, while surly describes a bad-tempered and unfriendly manner.

supplant|suppliant.distinction: To supplant is to push someone out and take their place, while a suppliant is one who begs humbly for a favour.

torpid|torrid.distinction: Torpid means sluggish to the point of dormancy, while torrid means burningly hot, or intensely passionate.

turbid|turgid.distinction: Turbid water is cloudy with sediment, while turgid prose is swollen and pompous; one is muddy, the other overblown.

usurp|usury.distinction: To usurp is to seize power you have no right to, while usury is the practice of lending money at extortionate interest.

venal|venial.distinction: Venal means open to bribery, which is a serious charge, while venial means minor and forgivable.

venal|vernal.distinction: Venal means corruptible by money, while vernal simply means belonging to the spring.

veracious|voracious.distinction: Veracious means truthful, while voracious means having a huge appetite, for food or for anything else.

xenophobia|xenophobic.distinction: Xenophobia is the fear or hatred of foreigners itself, while xenophobic is the adjective for a person or remark expressing it.
